services: Matins: God is the Lord, with four of this psalm's verses
The Matins of Pascha: verse 24, with Christ is risen

about.what: A psalm of thanksgiving, the hundred and seventeenth as the Church counts the psalms, by the Septuagint. It begins and ends with the same verse, “Give thanks to the Lord; for he is good: for his mercy endures for ever” (verses 1 and 29), and in it are “The stone which the builders rejected, the same is become the head of the corner” (verse 22) and “This is the day which the Lord has made: let us exult and rejoice in it” (verse 24), quoted here in Brenton's English.
about.history: The Church sings this psalm's verses in her services. At Matins the choir sings “God is the Lord”, from the psalm's verses 27 and 26, four times, and the deacon sets four of its verses between: verse 1, verse 10, verse 17, and verses 22 and 23 (Hapgood's Service Book, 1906, Matins, pp. 26 and 27). At the Matins of Pascha its verse 24 is one of the verses sung with “Christ is risen from the dead” (the same book, p. 226).
about.when: At Matins, after the Great Litany, with God is the Lord; and at the Matins of Pascha, with Christ is risen.

lines.en: Give thanks to the Lord; for he is good:
for his mercy endures for ever.
Alleluia.
Give thanks to the Lord; for he is good:
for his mercy endures for ever.
Alleluia.

lines.text: مِنَ ٱلضِّيقِ دَعَوْتُ ٱلرَّبَّ فَأَجَابَنِي مِنَ ٱلرُّحْبِ.
lines.translit: Mina d-diqi da'awtu r-Rabba fa-ajabani mina r-ruhbi.
lines.en: I called on the Lord out of affliction: and he hearkened to me, so as to bring me into a wide place.
for his mercy endures for ever.
Alleluia.
It is better to trust in the Lord
than to trust in man.
for his mercy endures for ever.
Alleluia.
It is better to hope in the Lord,
than to hope in princes.
for his mercy endures for ever.
Alleluia.

lines.text: قُوَّتِي وَتَرَنُّمِي ٱلرَّبُّ، وَقَدْ صَارَ لِي خَلَاصًا.
lines.translit: Quwwati wa-tarannumi r-Rabbu, wa-qad sara li khalasan.
lines.en: The Lord is my strength and my song, and is become my salvation.
lines.unsure: Heard only in part by the speech model; it wants a listener who knows Arabic.

lines.en: for his mercy endures for ever.
Alleluia.

lines.text: يَمِينُ ٱلرَّبِّ مُرْتَفِعَةٌ. يَمِينُ ٱلرَّبِّ صَانِعَةٌ بِبَأْسٍ.
lines.translit: Yaminu r-Rabbi murtafi'atun. Yaminu r-Rabbi sani'atun bi-ba'sin.
lines.en: The right hand of the Lord has exalted me: the right hand of the Lord has wrought powerfully.
for his mercy endures for ever.
Alleluia.

lines.text: تَأْدِيبًا أَدَّبَنِي ٱلرَّبُّ، وَإِلَى ٱلْمَوْتِ لَمْ يُسْلِمْنِي.
lines.translit: Ta'diban addabani r-Rabbu, wa-ila l-mawti lam yuslimni.
lines.en: The Lord has chastened me sore: but he has not given me up to death.
for his mercy endures for ever.
Alleluia.

lines.text: اِفْتَحُوا لِي أَبْوَابَ ٱلْبِرِّ. أَدْخُلْ فِيهَا وَأَحْمَدِ ٱلرَّبَّ.
lines.translit: Iftahu li abwaba l-birri. Adkhul fiha wa-ahmadi r-Rabba.
lines.en: Open to me the gates of righteousness: I will go into them, and give praise to the Lord.
for his mercy endures for ever.
Alleluia.

lines.text: هَذَا ٱلْبَابُ لِلرَّبِّ. ٱلصِّدِّيقُونَ يَدْخُلُونَ فِيهِ.
lines.translit: Hadha l-babu lir-Rabbi. As-siddiquna yadkhuluna fihi.
lines.en: This is the gate of the Lord: the righteous shall enter by it.
lines.unsure: Heard only in part by the speech model; it wants a listener who knows Arabic.

lines.en: for his mercy endures for ever.
Alleluia.

lines.text: أَحْمَدُكَ لِأَنَّكَ ٱسْتَجَبْتَ لِي وَصِرْتَ لِي خَلَاصًا.
lines.translit: Ahmaduka li-annaka stajabta li wa-sirta li khalasan.
lines.en: I will give thanks to thee; because thou hast heard me, and art become my salvation.
for his mercy endures for ever.
Alleluia.

lines.text: ٱلْحَجَرُ ٱلَّذِي رَفَضَهُ ٱلْبَنَّاؤُونَ قَدْ صَارَ رَأْسَ ٱلزَّاوِيَةِ.
lines.translit: Al-hajaru lladhi rafadahu l-banna'una qad sara ra'sa z-zawiyati.
lines.en: The stone which the builders rejected, the same is become the head of the corner.
for his mercy endures for ever.
Alleluia.

lines.text: مِنْ قِبَلِ ٱلرَّبِّ كَانَ هَذَا، وَهُوَ عَجِيبٌ فِي أَعْيُنِنَا.
lines.translit: Min qibali r-Rabbi kana hadha, wa-huwa 'ajibun fi a'yunina.
lines.en: This has been done of the Lord; and it is wonderful in our eyes.
for his mercy endures for ever.
Alleluia.

lines.text: هَذَا هُوَ ٱلْيَوْمُ ٱلَّذِي صَنَعُهُ ٱلرَّبُّ، نَبْتَهِجُ وَنَفْرَحُ فِيهِ.
lines.translit: Hadha huwa l-yawmu lladhi sana'ahu r-Rabbu, nabtahiju wa-nafrahu fihi.
lines.en: This is the day which the Lord has made: let us exult and rejoice in it.

lines.text: آهِ يَارَبُّ خَلِّصْ! آهِ يَارَبُّ أَنْقِذْ!
lines.translit: Ahi ya-Rabbu khallis! Ahi ya-Rabbu anqidh!
lines.en: O Lord, save now: O Lord, send now prosperity.
Thou art my God, and I will give thee thanks: thou art my God, and I will exalt thee.

lines.text: أَحْمَدُكَ لِأَنَّكَ ٱسْتَجَبْتَ لِي وَصِرْتَ لِي خَلَاصًا.
lines.translit: Ahmaduka li-annaka stajabta li wa-sirta li khalasan.
lines.en: I will give thanks to thee; because thou hast heard me, and art become my salvation.
Give thanks to the Lord; for he is good:
for his mercy endures for ever.
Alleluia.

variants.wordsSource: The whole of what the recording sings, printed from the Van Dyck Arabic Bible (1865, public domain; Psalm 118 in its count) verse by verse, in the order the soloist and the choir sing them: the first verse (by the soloist, then the choir), then the fifth, eighth, ninth, fourteenth, sixteenth, eighteenth to twenty-fifth, twenty-eighth, the twenty-first again, and the last, each followed by the first verse's refrain and hallelujah, in Van Dyck's own words and spelling. The verses and their order were heard in the recording by a speech model. Van Dyck's wording is printed as it is: where the singers' Arabic differs from it (the choir's first verse and verses 5, 8, 9, 16, 21, 22, 24, 25 and 28 are sung in other words), the line is Van Dyck's, not the words sung, and verses 14 and 20 were heard only in part. The English over each line is Brenton's for the same verse. Each line is timed to the recording. The transliteration is ours.
